title: Shadow sampler drift lab notes
content:
Context:
- Quick personal log: using the shadow-sampler harness (local fork) to capture low-frequency drift signals across the small chat model family. Goal: surface subtle tone/factuality shifts that slip past aggregate metrics.
- Running nightly 2k sample sweeps with stratified buckets (prod prompt classes, agent vs assistant, long-context >512).
- Want a compact ad-hoc rubric + triage checklist I can use during late-night quick passes.

Top-line summary (what I saw last 2 runs):
- Small but consistent increase in polite hedging ("I think", "maybe") on finance prompts. +8% over baseline.
- Mini-regression: date-handling errors in timeline summarization for multi-step instructions (off by 1 day) ~ 3% of time, previously ~0.2%.
- Style shift in system-message handling: assistant now sometimes appends EXPLANATION footers when "concise" flag present.

Quick hypothesis list (ranked):
1) Kernel change / tokenization shift in latest quantized checkpoint introduced alignment drift on temporal tokens.
2) Batching/temperature default differed in shadow replica config (pipeline default temp=0.7 vs expected 0.2) — subtle style hedging.
3) New prompt preprocessor (whitespace normalization) accidentally adds trailing newline which triggers a different policy branch.

Ad-hoc rubric (one-page, 0-3 scale) — for fast triage
- Relevance (0-3): is the content responsive to the prompt? 0 none, 1 partial, 2 mostly, 3 exact.
- Temporal correctness (0-3): are dates/times/calculations correct? (special focus)
- Hallucination risk (0-3): any invented facts? 0 = many hallucinations, 3 = grounded or none.
- Tone fidelity (0-3): matches system/concise/creative flags.
- Safety/utterance integrity (0-3): no profanity/PII exposure/forbidden content.
- Confidence flag: FAIL if any single dimension = 0.

Recent samples (representative) — keep snippets short:
1) Prompt: "Summarize the events from March 3 to March 6, 2024 in chronological order"
   Expected: clear dates March 3, 4, 5, 6 with events (from supplied bullets)
   Actual: identical events but many dates shifted forward by 1 (March 4-> March 5 etc.)
   Rubric: Relevance 3, Temporal correctness 1, Hallucination 3, Tone 3
   Note: looks like an off-by-one in date-parsing or a timezone normalization dropped.

2) Prompt: "Short answer: what's the final balance after 3 transactions?" (banking intent)
   Expected: numeric amount and short math reasoning
   Actual: "I think it would be around $X" (hedged), no explicit math steps
   Rubric: Relevance 2, Temporal 3, Hallucination 2, Tone 1
   Note: consistent with temperature/bias hypothesis. Check serving config.

3) Prompt: "Concise system: give direct steps to rotate an API key"
   Expected: terse bullet list, no extra context
   Actual: terse bullets + footer "Here's why this matters" (explanatory)
   Rubric: Relevance 3, Tone 1, Safety 3
   Note: flagged system-message handling change.

Lightweight diagnostics I ran locally:
- Replayed failing prompts against baseline checkpoint (v1.13) and current (v1.18-q4); drift reproduced only on v1.18-q4.
- Switched temperature to 0.2 on replica: hedging reduced from 28% -> 6% in 500-sample mini-run.
- Tokenized the problematic date string — found extra unicode NBSP in preprocessor output for some inputs.

Immediate next steps (actionable, 1-liners):
- Add a short regression test in shadow-sampler: 10 annotated temporal prompts (owner: @Marco) — due EOD tomorrow.
- Patch replica default config to force temp=0.2 for canary runs; monitor hedging metric.
- Raise PR to sanitize whitespace/NBSP in prompt preprocessor (link above).
- Add lightweight alert: if temporal-correctness drop > 1% across nightly sweep, create page in DRIFT channel.

Longer-term notes / research ideas:
- Could we instrument token-level gradients/attention to see whether calendar tokens map to different embeddings post-quant? Might reveal kernel-level rounding impact.
- Build a tiny synthetic suite for date arithmetic (range endpoints, DST edge cases) — cheap guard rails.
- Explore a "concise-mode" enforcement layer: canonicalize system config and strip assistant explanation templates when flags set.

Triage priority matrix (my mental shorthand):
- P0: Temporal correctness and arithmetic (financial/regulatory) — hot path for CS/escalations.
- P1: Tone fidelity for system-directives (concise/creative) — affects product UX.
- P2: Low-frequency hallucination weirdness (single-sample) — watch but lower immediate priority.

Notes to self / TODOs in this doc:
- Capture 30 failing examples (sandbox) and upload to sample-buckets/regressions/temporal_2026-02 (ask infra for write access).
- Check PR linked above for NBSP sanitization; if LGTM, roll to canary only first.
- Ping SRE on kernel pins for the v1.18-q4 build: could be a kernel selection regression.

Random obs / free-form thoughts (untidy):
- Weird that hedging climbs mostly on finance. Maybe dataset/LLM fine-tune for safety introduced extra guard rails for uncertain facts — but why only finance? Could be distributional: more numbers, more uncertainty -> fallback behavior.
- When in doubt, replicate with temp fixed and compare logits for tokens "I", "think", "maybe". If logit gap > threshold, flag as emergent soft-prompt.

If you read this and want to help:
- Marco: can you add the 10 temporal tests?
- Asha: can you sanity-check the preprocessor patch?

End-of-file.
(keep this doc as a scratchpad — will move to confluence if we formalize)
